title: Real reboot on a dedicated Linux host: every saved generation is reclaimed without a request
subtitle: PR #12869 · Ubuntu 24.04.4 LTS, kernel 6.8.0-117, ext4 · the real server jar under systemd + MySQL 8.4.11 + bundled worker · trusted-local-reboot-recovery=true · production HostIdentity.linux()

blocks.label: four reboots of the same machine (machine-id f03cd9a6… never changed)

blocks.pre:
R6 and R7 were hands-off: MySQL and the server came back through systemd/Docker restart policies.
R6: 21.0 s from the reboot command to the last RELEASED.   R7: 21 s from the power cut, 3.5 s after the server process started.

blocks.label: R7 at the PR head, arm by arm (SQL + durable registrations + /proc, read before the power cut and after the recovery)
table: after the reboot, no Broker request sent

READY, holder, escaped writer alive
1 SETTLED + 1 in-flight (EXECUTING) + 130 PREPARED

++ RELEASED  loss=trusted-host-reboot  stop=trusted-host-reboot
++ holder cleared · 131 ABANDONED without result · 1 SETTLED keeps its result
READY, holder, one polled in-flight call

READY, holder; then access revoked, Session DELETED,
Registry REMOVED/storage changed, mount removed from the config

worker SIGKILLed at 18:29:18: LOST, loss=registered-process-exit,
no stop evidence, holder pinned, escaped writer still writing
worker died before READY: RECOVERY_BLOCKED, no lease, no endpoint
binding warmed 18:29:36.239Z, 0.5 s before the power cut
++ registration survived the power loss · RELEASED

blocks.label: R7 totals
blocks.pre:
bindings      READY 5, LOST 1, RECOVERY_BLOCKED 1      ->  RELEASED 7
holders       5                                        ->  0
executions    nonterminal 132 (130 PREPARED, 2 EXECUTING) ->  0   (all ABANDONED, none replayed, none with a result)
registrations READY 5, RETIRED 2                       ->  RETIRED 7, each still carrying the ORIGINAL boot id 734e2d4c…
processes     5 workers, 2 escaped writers             ->  none; no worker was launched by the recovery

blocks.note: R1: the first in-guest reboot moved Docker's data root of this VM onto a fresh data disk, so the MySQL container (not its data directory, which sits on the root disk) had to be re-created by hand; the server crash-looped under systemd until the database answered at 17:51:34Z and then recovered in 4 s. R6 and R7 needed no manual step.
